title: Not Comfortable!
review_text:
Every breastfeeding Mom will find a time when she could use some thermal gel pads. Be it mastitis, engorgement, clogged ducts, or just sore breasts. I have used several brands of gel pads, having breastfed for quite some time.

I like the covers that come with these pads. The covers are very soft and nice. I like the idea of covering the gel pad.

It is the actual pad that is the problem. Not microwavable. (It takes quite some time and a bit of trial and error to get them warm enough to help.) This also makes them wet (you heat them in warm water) so you have to dry them before putting them into the cover. That doesn't seem like a big deal, but extra steps when you're dealing with breastfeeding issues are never helpful. The pad feels awful. It is harder plastic on the outside and thin, watery "gel" on the inside. (Much like a freezer pack to put in a cooler.) It has lots of plastic around the edges, so when you conform it to your breast, the plastic pokes and feels horrible. I think they were trying to go the right direction with the design, but missed the mark entirely with their choice of materials.
sentence: Every breastfeeding Mom will find a time when she could use some thermal gel pads.

title: Actually, pretty dang great.
review_text:
I didn't want to get this at first--we have seven strollers already! But my wife insisted and I thought, "Well, it seems more portable than our default portable one."
It's still bulky, and doesn't compact as much as other umbrella/folding strollers, but I'm a fan. Because this is the storage model, there is a TON of features on this thing, and enough compartments/doodads to hold our items while still being "compact" enough to throw comfortably into the trunk of a car.

Out of the box, some assembly is required. But the instructions are very easy to follow, and I had the stroller fully assembled in less than twenty minutes--no tools required. Everything is easily accessible (so far), and if you need to adjust the straps you can do so even while out and about.

The handles aren't adjustable, but they're actually at a really good angle and height so I can't complaint. More of a "casual" type of feel. However, after a couple of weeks of use, I've noticed that the grip is tending to slide down since it doesn't come over the tip of the handle and you really tend to push down while pushing the stroller. Also would've been nice if they curved the handles more. I've found that, when we have the stroller folded, we can't really push it along since it gets heavy as the handles don't hug the hand while being pushed (folded). We had an old, cheap folding stroller that was very easy to push when folded because I could let the hooks of the handles hang over my hands while I pushed it. Not so with this one. Sure, it comes with a shoulder sling to carry this, but it's pretty large and heavy that it gets heavy after a while.

The wheels do not turn very well, and I wish they would be rubber tires instead of plastic.

All in all, a very good stroller that's more portable than anything else we've owned. It's not perfectly portable, and this company makes more portable ones, but if you want one with lots of storage and compartments, while still being able to haul it on trains or in the back of the car, this one is it.

title: May not be for every kid, but works for ours.
review_text:
The Drop-Ins idea is great in itself, but we're unable to refrigerate these as we can other bottles. The breast milk begins to clot on the sides unless the milk is used right away.
My 2-month old daughter didn't initially like these, but after a couple more uses, we found that she had an easier time drinking from these than Similac or Medela's bottles, which are two of our other options. The Avent ones measure up nicely, but what we like about the Playtex Drop Ins is that our daughter won't suck in as much air as she might from other bottles.

Yes, they can measure expensively in the long run, but we'd prefer that over our daughter, who drinks a ton, drinking in too much air.

title: Keeps Babies Warm and it's Cute!
review_text:
Newborns have a few things in common and among them is the desire to stay warm. It’s important to make sure they are nice and snug and one easy way to achieve this need is with the Sumersault Deer Ivory 100% Cotton Wearable Blanket "Little Dreamer".

This wearable blanket scores well on the cuteness factor, with a small deer on the outside. The manufacturer makes these with other animals too, but I have the one with the deer. There is no need to worry about your baby’s reaction to the ink- the design is on the outside, so the skin won’t touch it.

Made from cotton, this wearable blanket is soft and babies will love the additional warmth it provides. One thing to keep in mind is that this is sleeveless, so it isn’t going to keep the arms warm. It’s meant to give babies a little more freedom of movement. You could still attempt to place their arms inside, but there is space for them to poke their arms back out.

With its full- length zipper, this wearable blanket is easy to take off and put back on. There are no legs, so a baby will easily lift right out and back in. A smart feature of the design is that the dipper is inverted. This keeps it away from a baby’s face, for added safety.

Babies get fussy when they are cold. Sumersault Deer Ivory 100% Cotton Wearable Blanket eliminates this problem, providing the extra warmth a baby needs to get through the night. You could even eliminate a regular blanket and just use this, depending on circumstances and temps in the room. It’s a useful and cute item for babies and makes a great gift for parents.
sentence: It's important to make sure they are nice and snug and one easy way to achieve this need is with the Sumersault Deer Ivory 100% Cotton Wearable Blanket

Newborns have a few things in common and among them is the desire to stay warm. It’s important to make sure they are nice and snug and one easy way to achieve this need is with the Sumersault Deer Ivory 100% Cotton Wearable Blanket "Little Dreamer".

This wearable blanket scores well on the cuteness factor, with a small deer on the outside. The manufacturer makes these with other animals too, but I have the one with the deer. There is no need to worry about your baby’s reaction to the ink- the design is on the outside, so the skin won’t touch it.

Made from cotton, this wearable blanket is soft and babies will love the additional warmth it provides. One thing to keep in mind is that this is sleeveless, so it isn’t going to keep the arms warm. It’s meant to give babies a little more freedom of movement. You could still attempt to place their arms inside, but there is space for them to poke their arms back out.

With its full- length zipper, this wearable blanket is easy to take off and put back on. There are no legs, so a baby will easily lift right out and back in. A smart feature of the design is that the dipper is inverted. This keeps it away from a baby’s face, for added safety.

Babies get fussy when they are cold. Sumersault Deer Ivory 100% Cotton Wearable Blanket eliminates this problem, providing the extra warmth a baby needs to get through the night. You could even eliminate a regular blanket and just use this, depending on circumstances and temps in the room. It’s a useful and cute item for babies and makes a great gift for parents.
sentence: One thing to keep in mind is that this is sleeveless, so it isn't going to keep the arms warm.

title: Very high quality bag
review_text:
With four kids, we have gone through MANY diaper bags during the years. This is absolutely one of the highest quality ones I have found. You can just tell by how it feels. It definitely feels thicker and more durable, which is very important.

The bag has an overall nice look. It's not as stylish as some of mine, but one thing that the husbands will appreciate is that it is much more gender neutral than a lot of the others. title: Nice Bassinet--needs better "mattress"
review_text: This bassinet is really, really easy to set up. I was very impressed with that. It also seems very sturdy. I'm really concerned about the "mattress" pad it came with, though. I have diaper changing pads and quilts that have more cushion. There are warnings against using any other padding due to suffocation risks and I respect that. However, my baby isn't here yet, so I don't know how she'd react to sleeping on a particle board slat covered with a thin blanket. I can't imagine it will be good. The zippered cover is odd, but we camp frequently and I can see it being very useful...in the woods. I'm not foreseeing any mosquitoes in my house, though. Even though I sound a little negative, I recommended this to my sister who is having a baby a month after me. She bought one and was also impressed with the weight, construction, and ease of set up...but concerned with the so-called mattress. The colors are cute and as I mentioned earlier, it's very sturdy and easy to set up, take down, or fold. It's compact and lightweight and I'm excited to travel with it rather than our huge playpen. The only thing keeping me from a five star rating is that darn mattress pad.
sentence: This bassinet is really, really easy to set up.

title: Useful for kittens
review_text:
I've raised 7 kittens with these over the past few years I knew of their existence. They're smaller and softer, so kittens adjust to them a little easier than an off the shelf rubber nipple from the pet store. It's also easier for the more narrow mouthed to form a good latch, which is ideal to avoid aspiration complications.

These saved their teeny lives and I still have some tucked away in case another needs help. It's also a great donation item for any neonatal kitten center at a shelter if you have one, which I unfortunately don't have. Overall, highly recommend for those who rescue, foster, and/or find neonatal kittens.

title: It doesn't look like a diaper bag
review_text: I bought this for my son who has special needs. Usually diaper bags are for babies so little ducks or pink teddy bears would be appropriate. It still has all of the best features like a wipes pocket on the outside for easy access and a waterproof interior. There's an insulated section for snacks or drinks and enough pockets for everything he could possibly need on an outing. It's gender neutral so it works great for boys and girls. It would also be a nice diaper bag for a daddy.
sentence: I bought this for my son who has special needs.
aspect: price, cost and value for money

title: Great pump even after much use
review_text:
I bought this pump after getting the S2 from insurance, so I could have one at home and one at the office. It also gave me the extra set of pump parts I needed without having to buy them separately. I have been using them for over 10 months (5 times a day during the week) and have had no problems.

I leave this one at home, where I sometimes use the battery for convenience, and I don't need the battery at work, where I only pump at my desk.

The only real difference I have seen between the two, othan than the battery capability with the S1, is the S1 is slightly noisier, though not enough to make a difference. When the tubing is not connected, the S1 (but not S2) is quite loud, so I thought the first one I got was defective. Once you put the tubing on, it is fine.

The only downside for me has been that when I have needed to order additional pump parts, I could not just buy them in a store (or even the city breastfeeding center). I assume that will change as Spectra becomes more common, but for now, ordering from the manufacturer is the only real option for replacement parts. I did buy another company's duckbills, though, and they worked fine despite looking different.
sentence: I bought this pump after getting the S2 from insurance, so I could have one at home and one at the office.
aspect: price, cost and value for money
